narr: A slow moving cold front drifted south across East Texas and North Louisiana south of the Interstate 20 corridor during the morning hours of April 6th. Abundant moisture from the Gulf and the Southern Pacific continued to stream northeast along and behind the front, south of an upper low that shifted northeast into the Central Plains. This moisture enhanced rain rates, with embedded thunderstorms developing and moving repeatedly over the same areas. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-5 inches fell across much of Deep East Texas and Northwest Louisiana from the 5th to the 7th, atop already saturated grounds from much above normal rainfall received during the winter and early springtime months. This resulted in areas of flash flooding across portions of Bossier and Desoto Parishes, before the rains gradually ended as the front shifted south out of the area and drier air spilled south in its wake.
